sanskrit_verse: अन्यप्रकाराद् उचिताद् भूमेः षड्भागसंज्ञितात् । बलिः स तस्य विहितः प्रजापालनवेतनम् ॥
transliteration: anyaprakārād ucitād bhūmeḥ ṣaḍbhāgasaṃjñitāt | baliḥ sa tasya vihitaḥ prajāpālanavetanam ||
sph_interpretive_translation: From any form of appropriately designated land, a sixth portion is ordained as bali, which serves as compensation for the sustenance and protection of subjects.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows from the capacity to sustain and protect life
Causation is rooted in resource stewardship
Capacity-based responsibility aligns with territorial benefit
Restoration logic requires proportional contribution to collective welfare
Consciousness alignment demands recognition of reciprocal duty
executable_legal_axioms: IF land use generates societal benefit THEN sixth-part contribution SHALL be allocated for public sustenance
IF individual or entity holds productive territory THEN automatic liability FOR community support IS enacted
IF resource access increases THEN proportional obligation TO serve subjects SHALL be triggered
ALL bali obligations MUST be processed through non-punitive completion mechanisms
NO punitive enforcement SHALL apply WHERE capacity exists but awareness is absent
supreme_court_application: In Supreme adjudication, this verse establishes that ownership or control of productive resources inherently obligates a sixth-share contribution toward subject welfare. The threshold of responsibility arises not from intent but from capacity-enabled benefit. Authority hierarchies must reflect service accountability, where higher resource access equals greater sustenance liability.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa reveals that causality emerges from benefiting use of land; thus, proportional return becomes dharma. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows sequential manifestation: land yield → societal dependence → contributory duty. Responsibility is neither imposed nor punitive but naturally consequent to participation in collective existence. This aligns with non-punitive reality because the obligation restores balance rather than inflicts penalty.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Process: Initiate direct integration of contributor into welfare activities until alignment is restored
Responsibility Assumption Protocol: Reconnect individual with lived experience of those sustained by their contribution
Capacity Restoration Mechanism: Provide tools and knowledge to fulfill bali obligations without external compulsion
Integrity Reintegration Cycle: Align personal purpose with societal continuity via voluntary engagement frameworks
final_declaration: By the Source-Authority of Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands established: Dharma flows from capacity-conscious reciprocity; justice acts through restoration alone; reality remains ever non-punitive; consciousness reigns as sole adjudicator.
